item.title: Study on the evolution of division of labor patterns and interaction mechanisms in organized interdisciplinary collaboration
item.description: Organized interdisciplinary research collaboration is a crucial measure for advancing the national strategy of building a leading-edge science and technology power. However, organized interdisciplinary collaboration still faces challenges, such as unclear theoretical mechanisms for collaborative interaction (Zhao Lanxiang et al., 2024) and difficulties in reconciling diverse disciplinary perspectives in practice. Relevant research has lagged behind in addressing issues related to the division of labor and its underlying mechanisms, which severely limits the synergistic innovation potential of organized interdisciplinary collaboration. To implement the requirements of the Ministry of Science and Technology and other departments regarding strengthening the organized research system, transforming the research paradigm, and enhancing multi-actor collaboration, this study focuses on the perspective of the division of labor in research. It innovatively constructs an analytical framework for the division of labor patterns and a model for examining collaboration mechanisms in organized interdisciplinary research. By integrating natural language processing techniques and causal analysis, this study systematically reveals the characteristics of the division of labor and its dynamic evolution patterns among different research entities in various interdisciplinary contexts. The aim is to break through traditional thinking and provide theoretical foundations and practical strategies for the management and implementation of organized interdisciplinary collaboration.

item.title: Contributorship in Scientific Collaborations: The Perspective of Contribution-based Byline Orders
A study on the causal effect of research team diversity on research performance
item.description: In light of the increasingly intense international competition in science and technology and the opportunities presented by domestic reforms in science and technology evaluation, this project, based on a massive dataset of academic publications, investigates the characteristics and spatial-temporal distribution patterns of team diversity in scientific collaboration. Furthermore, it explores the causal relationship between team diversity and the research performance of both teams and individuals, aiming to provide a research foundation for effective team formation and optimization, and for the rational allocation of research resources. Through a systematic review of relevant research literature and data on scientific collaboration, this project will develop a multi-dimensional framework for characterizing team diversity, creating a comprehensive profile of research teams based on their diversity. Using spatial-temporal analysis tools, it will examine the distribution and evolution patterns of team diversity in real-world research collaborations, and explore the factors influencing team diversity. Finally, it will analyze the causal effects of team diversity on the research performance of both teams and individual researchers. This research will deepen our understanding of scientific collaboration, accurately assess the impact of team diversity on research outcomes, and provide policy recommendations and practical suggestions for building and optimizing research teams and for the rational allocation of research resources.

item.title: Study of Scientific Collaborators' Scientific Effectiveness from The Perspective of Division of Labor
item.description: Situated in the increasingly fierce international scientific and technological competition and Seizing the opportunity for reforming domestic scientific and technological evaluation system, this project takes the division of labor and roles of scientific research as a start point to explore the phenomenon of division of labor, the evolving rule of scientific collaborating roles and the scientific effectiveness in scientific collaboration. We further explore the causal relationship between the role classification of scientific collaborators and their scientific effectiveness, to optimize the evaluation of scientific effectiveness of scientific collaborators, enhance the willingness of scientists to collaborate, and promote scientific collaboration. This project combines the theory of team effectiveness and the practice of scientific collaboration to build an indicator system of scientific effectiveness, evaluate the scientific effectiveness of scientific collaborators, and use the author ’s contribution statement in the scientific literature to build a co-contributorship network(constructed by the collaborators having completed tasks together in their teams), to detect the division of labor in scientific collaboration and the evolving rule of collaborating roles, and use causal analysis to measure the relationship between collaborating roles and the scientific effectiveness in scientific collaborations. This research can deeply understand the phenomenon of scientific collaboration, accurately assess the scientific effectiveness of scientific collaborators, and help to optimize the evaluating methods of scientific collaboration, establish a new type of scientific research evaluation system, and cultivate a good innovation environment.
